title: Exit path mapping & counterfactual playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
A tactical template for mapping how accounts exit (the "exit path"), capturing evidence, and enumerating counterfactual interventions we could have taken to alter the outcome. Intended for CS leads, AMs, product partners and SRE when conducting a loss review after renewal decline or cancellation.

Scope and usage notes:
- Use this for any account loss where ARR >= $20k or strategic importance is medium/ high.
- Complementary to the standard postmortem; this doc emphasizes the decision points and what changes (people/process/product) could have changed the decision.
- Keep it short and evidence-driven: owners should fill the timeline first, then hypotheses and counterfactuals.

Quick checklist (start here):
1) Populate timeline (key interactions, contract milestones, feature asks) — owner: AM
2) Attach customer quotes / emails and product tickets — owner: CS Ops
3) Rate each root cause hypothesis (Impact x Confidence) — owner: CS lead
4) For top hypotheses, list concrete counterfactuals and what would be required to run A/B or pilot tests — owner: Solutions Eng + PM
5) Decide 3 prevention actions + owners and due dates — owner: Head of CS

Sections (fill sequentially):
1) Executive summary (2–3 lines)
- One-line reason the account left (customer language preferred)
- High-level ARR / product footprint / renewal date

2) Account context (facts)
- Industry, ARR, deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), region
- Primary contact and champion, procurement contact, legal reviewer
- Contract cadence and notice deadlines

3) Timeline of critical events (record dates, channel, owner)
- YYYY-MM-DD: Renewal discussion #1 — Notes: champion requested dedicated throughput guarantee; AM proposed Dedicated plan; ticket #1234 created
- YYYY-MM-DD: Support incident (sev2) — KV cache bug caused 30% latency spike for a key route; mitigation: rollback config; incident ticket #S-987
- YYYY-MM-DD: Procurement pricing counterproposal received (30% reduction request)
- YYYY-MM-DD: Final decision communicated (churn notice sent)

4) Evidence pack (paste or link raw artifacts)
- Links to Slack threads, email threads, Zoom notes, support tickets, SLO dashboards, performance traces
- Key customer quotes (verbatim, with date)

5) Root-cause hypotheses (short bullets)
For each hypothesis, include: statement, evidence, impact score (1–5), confidence (1–5), suggested owner to investigate.
- Hypothesis A: "Performance variability on peak traffic eroded trust in SLA" — Evidence: S-987 + latency dashboards + customer quote; Impact 5; Confidence 4; Owner: SRE/serving-runtime
- Hypothesis B: "Billing/pricing misalignment for bulk-embedding use case" — Evidence: Procurement email + usage spike in billing export; Impact 4; Confidence 3; Owner: RevOps + Pricing
- Hypothesis C: "Feature mismatch: missing structured output hooks for tool-calling workflow" — Evidence: Product feedback doc; Impact 3; Confidence 2; Owner: Product-hosted-api

6) Counterfactual scenarios (what concrete intervention would plausibly change the decision?)
For each top hypothesis, list 2–3 counterfactuals and feasibility notes. Also indicate the minimum signal that would indicate the counterfactual could work (success metric).
- For Hypothesis A (performance variability):
  - CF-A1: "Dedicated capacity pilot with guaranteed throughput SLA for 3 months" — Required: Priority queue on GPU pool, contractual SLA, price discount 15% for pilot; Feasibility: medium; Success metric: <P95 latency target met for 90% of windows for test routes; Time to run: 8 weeks
  - CF-A2: "Proactive monitoring + 24/7 SRE runbook with dedicated tracer for customer routes" — Required: SRE on-call rotation, trace instrumentation; Feasibility: high (ops cost); Success metric: incident count reduction to <=1 per month; Time: 4 weeks
- For Hypothesis B (pricing):
  - CF-B1: "Custom usage-based tier with committed-credits + overage protection" — Required: Pricing approval, billing integration; Feasibility: low-to-medium; Success metric: customer acceptance of 12-month commitment at 70% of requested discount; Time: 6 weeks

7) Counterfactual experiment design notes (if we wanted to test):
- Population: similar accounts (industry, usage pattern) n=8 with renewal in next 90 days
- Randomization: offer half a pilot vs. standard renewal messaging
- Outcome metrics: renewal rate lift, net revenue retention, incident frequency, NPS delta
- Minimum detectable effect and sample-size notes (attach calculations in linked_artifacts)

8) Customer reaction & objections log (chronological)
- Capture exact phrasing where possible and tag which team heard it (AM / Legal / Procurement)

9) Failure modes for each CF (what could go wrong if we run it)
- CF-A1 failure mode: resource contention leads to impacted customers; mitigation: capped pilot pool, strong gating
- CF-B1 failure mode: creates new discount channel that leaks—mitigation: strict eligibility + review

10) Prevention & remediation playbook (3 prioritized actions)
- Action 1 (High priority): "Performance guarantee pilot template" — Owner: Head of Redwood Dedicated; Due: 2026-04-01; Rationale: directly addresses top hypothesis; Dependencies: legal, capacity plan, pricing
- Action 2 (Medium): "Billing clarity packet and usage analytics export for AMs" — Owner: RevOps; Due: 2026-03-15; Rationale: reduces negotiation friction; Dependencies: BI dev time
- Action 3 (Low): "Product spec for structured tool-calling hooks" — Owner: Product-hosted-api; Due: 2026-06-30; Rationale: medium-term feature gap

11) Signals to monitor (what success looks like company-wide)
- Decreased renewal declines citing performance by X% quarter over quarter
- Reduced average time-to-remediate sev2s for key routes to < 6 hours
- Increased conversion when offering dedicated-pilot by +15pp

12) Communications plan (how we talk about learnings internally and to customers)
- Internal: 30-minute loss-review with CS, product, SRE; summarize in Confluence; share highlights at weekly GTM sync
- Customer-facing: one-page summary offered to at-risk customers explaining pilot path and safeguards

13) Ownership & next steps (table-style line items)
- Owner: Head of CS — Deliverable: finalize pilot contract template — Due: 2026-03-01
- Owner: SRE Lead — Deliverable: route-level SLA playbook — Due: 2026-03-10
- Owner: RevOps — Deliverable: pricing packet + billing export — Due: 2026-03-15

Appendix: Short templates to paste into emails / pilot offers:
- "We'd like to propose a 3-month dedicated throughput pilot with a measured SLA and a structured rollback clause. If the pilot meets the performance goals we will extend a committed capacity discount. Interested in a conversation next week to scope?"

Notes to the reviewer (internal):
- This is intentionally prescriptive: aim to surface interventions that could be operationalized within 6–12 weeks.
- For every loss we should attempt at least one counterfactual that is operationally realistic (low-to-medium lift) to evaluate in the next quarter.
- Attachments that should accompany this doc: latency traces, billing export CSV, contract redline, recent QBR slides.

Status: Draft — ready for AM + SRE inputs.
